findings.text: Ask 4 (the graph) is missing. The diff has no dashboard or Live-card change at all, only `GET /api/processes` (Servex/Servex.js:590). plan.md step 3 ("the graph on the Live card … a screenshot at 1920") was not delivered, and the review has no screenshot. Servex/doc/processes.md:17 and :52 say "The Live card draws it", which is untrue until the graph ships.

Ask 1 says "wherever the dashboards list running agents, base it on actual claude.exe processes". No dashboard reads the new `running[].pid` / `lost` yet (Servex/Processes.js:195). The data exists, but the owner still sees nothing new. The same UI step should show the worktree count, which today appears only in `system_health` (Worktrees.js:193), not "on the process monitor" as the ask says.

Ask 1 also says to log the PID. In proof.txt line 8, "minion-tasked's log:" is empty, so the proof never showed the `{type: "process", state: "started", pid}` line (Agents.js:247) landing in the agent's log. Either the proof reads the wrong path (proof.mjs:61) or the event is not written. Show one real line before landing.

Ask 6 (the architect uses it) is covered only by adding the process line to the `system_health` verdict (Servex.js:696-699). The servex-mastermind and fans skills are unchanged. A one-line pointer in each skill to `/api/processes` and the orphan count would close the ask.

Appending the process line to `health().verdict` (Servex.js:699) changes a string other code may treat as the monitor's verdict, such as the flag message. A separate `processes.line` field is already returned, so the verdict could stay as it was.

Simpler: plan.md says the monitor's existing PowerShell loop would also read the process table ("No new PowerShell starts per sample"). Processes.js:84 starts a second long-lived PowerShell instead, so two samplers now poll the machine.

Worktrees.js:203 counts every new untracked file under `public/framework/ai/` as log noise, so a worktree whose real, uncommitted task files (plan.md, page.js) sit there gets `--force` removed. They are salvaged first (Worktrees.js:60), so nothing is lost, but they end up in `salvage/` where nobody will look. Consider treating only `*.jsonl` and images as noise.

The proof's live run (proof.txt, "+129s reaped by this Servex … 10") killed 8 real waiters that belonged to other sessions, after only 60 s idle. The default is 10 minutes, and the Git `ps -e` parent check looks right, but the first production start will reap in bulk. Worktrees.js `start()` will also remove every already-merged worktree (about 17) in its first pass, 2 minutes after start. Say both in the landing report so the owner is not surprised.

The sorting, reaping and noise rules are well covered by Servex/processes.test.mjs. The claude.exe PID matched Task Manager for both minions (proof.txt, "+30s … MATCH"). The core of asks 1, 2, 3 and 5 works.

answer.reply: fixing: the graph is merge 2, built by minion-process-graph from graph-brief.md; the doc no longer says the Live card draws it until it does (23637d01).
fixing in merge 2: Running now rows show pid and MB from running[], a lost badge, and the worktree count (graph-brief.md, part 2).
fixed: the proof read agent logs under the wrong name; the real lines from the same run are now in proof.txt ({type: process, state: started, pid: 47356}) and proof.mjs reads agent-<id>.jsonl.
sent: skills belong to the Servex mastermind, so the one-line pointers for servex-mastermind and fans went to it as a recommendation.
declined: nothing parses health().verdict (grep finds no reader); the flag message is built in Monitor.up() from its own reason. The appended line is what the architect should see first.

declined: a second loop on purpose. The monitor's loop runs every 5 s and must stay near-free (it gates spawns); the full process table with parents costs 0.2 s, so it runs every 10 s on its own. plan.md said otherwise; the doc's Cost section is the truth.
fixed: an untracked file under ai/ is noise only when it is a screenshot; a new plan.md or page.js keeps the worktree as uncommitted (test added).

noted for the landing: the first live pass reaps the leftover waiters and, 2 minutes after start, removes every finished worktree that has been quiet 2 hours. Also fixed on the way: our own git status refreshed the index and would have kept every worktree 'in use' forever (--no-optional-locks).
noted: skills belong to the Servex mastermind; the one-line pointers for servex-mastermind and fans were sent to it as a recommendation.
